summary.headline: Senco Gold Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY, but Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 4.4%; H1 EBITDA margin was 7.6% and H1 PAT 3.7%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 34% YoY in Q2 and 52% in H1, with H1 sales crossing INR 5,000 crores and TTM sales exceeding INR 10,000 crores. Margins were the weak point: Q2 EBITDA margin was 4.4% and Q2 PAT margin 4.1%, while H1 EBITDA margin of 7.6% sat within the 7.5%–7.8% guidance and H1 PAT margin of 3.7% was below the 4%–4.5% guided range. Management attributed the Q2 compression to customer-acquisition discounts and schemes (Flexi Gold, MariGold), old gold exchange (now ~51% of business), festive inventory build for franchisees, and hedging on a falling gold price. Dhanteras-period trading was strong, with revenue up ~25%–26% over 1 October–11 November. Management guided Q3 revenue growth of at least 25% and Q4 of at least 20%.

segments.name: Retail (COCO and franchise)
segments.commentary: Retail revenue grew ~29% in Q2 with SSSG of 19% in value. 14 stores opened in H1 and 10 more between 1 October and mid-November, taking FY27 openings to 24 against an 18–20 target; 3–4 more planned in the next 3–4 months.

segments.name: Diamond / studded jewellery
segments.commentary: H1 stud ratio ~11.6%; Dhanteras-period stud ratio ~9.5%–10% versus bars and coins ~7%. Diamond jewellery sales grew ~26% over the last 41 days. Management expects stud ratio to return to ~12% in Dec–Feb.

segments.name: East India
segments.commentary: East India contributes ~80% of revenue per management. Expansion focus is East, North, West, Central, with limited southern presence.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 revenue growth of at least 25% YoY; Q4 at least 20% YoY.
EBITDA margin guidance of 7.5%–7.8% retained; management expects Q2 EBITDA divergence to correct in Q3.
Sustainable growth of ~15%–16% in a stable gold-price scenario (SSSG 10%–12% plus 4%–5% from new stores).
Long-term vision: INR 20,000 crores revenue, 8% EBITDA margin and ~15% stud ratio; average sales per store could nearly double in 3–4 years.
Hedging at ~50% under board policy; intent to move toward 65%–70% once gold prices stabilise.
Gold metal loan share of working-capital borrowings expected to rise over the next 3–4 months as availability has stabilised.
capex_capacity: 14 new stores in H1 and 10 more from 1 October to mid-November, total 24 in FY27 against 18–20 target.
3–4 additional stores planned over the next 3–4 months.
Inventory up ~INR 200 crores versus March 2026, pertaining to 7 COCO stores.
Average sales per store expected to nearly double over 3–4 years; Delhi NCR described as the crown of pan-India strategy.
Franchise stores being expanded alongside COCO for Tier 2–4 penetration.
demand_pricing: Dhanteras-period revenue growth ~25%–26% from 1 October to 11 November (41 days), turnover crossed ~INR 2,400 crores; SSSG ~17%.
Average weight range per purchase down 10%–12% YoY as consumers prefer lighter jewellery; ticket sizes up.
Old gold exchange ~51% of business; reduces margin by ~20–40 bps according to management.
Unorganised players, aided by high duty, are discounting and driving price competition; management expects this to be short-lived.
Festive new customer acquisition up 30%; customer mix ~40%–45% new and ~55%–60% repeat.
Customer advances (Flexi Gold, MariGold) of ~INR 700–800 crores on the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin volatile quarter to quarter and what concrete steps will fix it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to H1 EBITDA of 7.6% within guidance, cited discounts, schemes and innovation launched to keep growing, and said consistency will improve over time as diamond mix and franchise share rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income rise sharply, and what is in it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other income is mainly net hedging gains (INR 99.9 crores) taken to protect cash flow against customer offers, described as one-off; regular FD and securities income is INR 35–40 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and impact of old gold exchange on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging is ~50% under board policy, targeting 65%–70% over time. Old gold exchange reduces margin by ~20–40 bps due to handling cost, melting losses and opportunity loss.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gold metal loan share fallen to 17% of working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GML availability was uncertain in Apr–May amid gold import curbs and GST issues at banks; this stabilised in Q2, and GML share is expected to rise while working-capital loans fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the vision for FY30 and how will growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from INR 10,000 crores to INR 20,000 crores is expected from SSSG (existing stores outside Bengal) and ~70 stores; focus regions are East, North, West and Central.

qa_highlights.question: How will the business perform with flat gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management models 10%–12% SSSG plus 4%–5% from new stores, i.e., ~15%–16% sustainable growth in a stable gold-price scenario, with share shifting to organised players.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Melorra and lab-grown diamonds?
qa_highlights.answer: Melorra is a collaboration to be a flanker brand for new-generation customers with lightweight and studded designs; 9-carat and 14-carat demand and lab-grown studded jewellery are rising.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Q3 and Q4 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided at least 25% growth for Q3 and at least 20% for Q4, citing Dhanteras performance.

risks_watch: Margin volatility: Q2 EBITDA 4.4% versus H1 7.6%; H1 PAT 3.7% below 4%–4.5% guidance. Watch whether Q3 EBITDA recovers into the 7.5%–7.8% range.
Other income quality: PAT was supported by hedging gains (INR 99.9 crores net), which management called one-off; hedging losses if gold rises are not discussed.
Unorganised competition using discounts; duration of price pressure is uncertain.
Operating cash flow negative in the period due to shift from gold metal loans to cash credit and CP; watch GML share recovery.
Inventory growth (~INR 200 crores since March 2026) versus cash conversion cycle.
Weight-range decline (10%–12%) and stud ratio falling to 9.5%–10% in the festive period versus ~12% target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and the Q3 outlook, but defensive and evasive on margin volatility, hedging detail and share price questions, repeatedly redirecting to H1 figures and long-term strategy.
key_quotes: We made deep investments in marketing and customer footfall to maintain the momentum, and we grew 34% Y-o-Y in Q2.
We are confident that this short-term divergent trend which you are seeing in Q2, in terms of EBITDA, will be corrected in Q3.
So, there is a net impact of around INR18 crores due to this hedging position in quarter one and quarter two.
50% is something that we shall continue to sustain, though our endeavour is to take it more than 50% towards 65%-70% over a period of time, once the gold prices stabilise.

adds.what: 24 new stores in FY27 (14 in H1 plus 10 from 1 Oct to mid-Nov) against 18-20 target
3-4 additional stores planned over next 3-4 months

growth.why: Management guides Q3 revenue growth of at least 25% and Q4 of at least 20%, plus sustainable ~15%-16% growth (SSSG 10-12% plus 4-5% from new stores), backed by Dhanteras-period revenue up ~25-26% and 24 new stores opened in FY27 against an 18-20 target, though no capacity or order figures beyond store count were given.

oneOffs.what: INR 30 crores customs duty gain in Q2 FY27 (INR 46 crores in H1, ~90 bps of H1 EBITDA); supports profit, not revenue
INR 99.9 crores net other income, mainly hedging gains that management called one-off; flatters PAT in H1 (PAT H1 INR 188 cr, ~22% growth)

quality.why: Revenue growth of 34% in Q2 (52% in H1) is driven by store expansion (24 openings), ~29% retail growth and ~19% same-store value growth, so the top line is largely organic; but profit growth is flattered by INR 99.9 crore of one-off hedging-related other income and INR 46 crore of H1 customs duty gains, while Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 4.4%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA fell to 4.4% against H1 7.6% and guided 7.5%-7.8%; management expects the Q2 divergence to correct in Q3, though discounts and old gold exchange (~51% of business, -20 to -40 bps) are headwinds.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 24 stores opened in FY27 (14 in H1, 10 from 1 Oct to mid-Nov) against an 18-20 target, with 3-4 more planned over the next 3-4 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q3 revenue growth guided at least 25% and Q4 at least 20%, with Dhanteras-period revenue up ~25-26% and sustainable growth of ~15-16% (SSSG 10-12% plus 4-5% from new stores).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q3 guided at least 25% and Q4 at least 20% after Dhanteras growth of ~25-26%, but the guide is a floor and margin recovery is not yet proven.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 PAT margin of 3.7% fell below the 4%-4.5% guide and Q2 EBITDA was 4.4%; the Q3 margin correction is not yet visible and unorganised players are discounting.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Melorra flanker brand for new-generation customers and rising lab-grown studded demand were discussed, but no launch date or revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Hedging gains and unorganised price competition
rows.why: Other income of INR 99.9 crores (mainly hedging gains, called one-off) flattered PAT, while unorganised players' discounting is seen as short-lived by management but is pressuring margins now.

rows.label: Gold metal loan share recovery
rows.why: GML availability stabilised in Q2 and management expects its share of working-capital borrowings to rise from 17%, while operating cash flow was negative in the period.

rows.label: Dhanteras and festive demand momentum
rows.why: Revenue up ~25-26% over 1 Oct to 11 Nov (41 days), turnover above INR 2,400 crores and SSSG ~17%, supporting the Q3 guide.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line momentum, Dhanteras growth and the Q3 outlook, but defensive and evasive on Q2 margin compression, hedging detail and the one-off other income; analysts pressed on margin volatility and PAT quality.
